title: PHAYZ
summary: A custom Next.js storefront for a t-shirt and hoodie brand, built with an in-house product customization tool, Razorpay payments, and a purpose-built admin CMS for catalog, orders, and customer management.
challenge: The brand needed more than a standard storefront — customers wanted to personalize hoodies with their own designs across front, back, and side print zones. Off-the-shelf platforms couldn't support this without heavy workarounds, and a generic CMS wasn't flexible enough for a product catalog built around configurable print zones and customer uploads.
solution: I built the storefront end-to-end in Next.js, with a canvas-based customization tool letting customers upload, position, rotate, and flip artwork within fixed print zones per garment. Payments run through Razorpay with webhook-verified order confirmation, automatic invoicing, and email notifications. A custom admin CMS handles the full operational surface — products, images, pricing, customer records, orders, wishlists, tags, and payment reconciliation.
impact: A customization flow customers can use without design experience
Reliable payment-to-fulfillment pipeline with webhook-verified order status
Single admin dashboard covering catalog, orders, and customers
A reusable CMS architecture ready to extend to future client projects
outcomes: Razorpay payment flow with webhook verification and automated invoicing
Purpose-built admin CMS for products, orders, and customers

title: Tej Computer Services
summary: One of the Largest trusted distributors for premium computer hardware, gaming accessories and tech solutions in the entire state of Jharkhand, India
challenge: The WordPress theme was slow, hard to extend, and fighting the brand. Merchandisers relied on familiar CMS workflows, but shoppers hit sluggish pages and a confusing path to purchase. A full platform migration was off the table — content and catalog needed to stay in WordPress.
solution: WordPress stayed as the backend for products, content, and editorial control. I rebuilt the customer-facing experience in Next.js with synced catalog data, clearer product discovery, and a tighter checkout path. The team kept their publishing habits; customers got a faster, calmer storefront.
impact: Noticeably faster browse and product pages
Clearer path from discovery to checkout
Merchandising workflows unchanged for the client team
A frontend stack ready for future campaigns and A/B tests
outcomes: Headless WordPress content and catalog sync
Faster product discovery and checkout path
CMS workflows unchanged for the client team

title: Kanke General Hospital & Research Centre
summary: A modern hospital website focused on trust, clarity, and conversion — with a prominent appointment path, department discovery, and content the clinical team can keep current.
challenge: The hospital needed a digital presence that felt as capable as their care — not a generic template. Patients had to find doctors, services, and a clear way to book or enquire quickly, while staff needed a site that stayed professional across mobile and desktop without constant developer edits for routine updates.
solution: I designed and built a dark, cinematic healthcare site with a strong hero, glass-style enquiry form, and direct appointment CTAs. Navigation covers departments, doctors, gallery, and contact in a calm hierarchy. The layout emphasizes immediate action — book or submit a query — while imagery and typography establish clinical trust.
impact: Clear first-screen path to book or enquire
Mobile-ready experience for patients searching on the go
A visual identity that matches modern hospital standards
Structured pages ready for doctors, services, and content growth
outcomes: Hero-led brand site with appointment and enquiry flows
Polished responsive UI tuned for healthcare trust
